message.content:
There isn’t actually a “Best Album” category at the Grammys—the top honor for an LP is **“Album of the Year.”**  
At the 59th Annual Grammy Awards (which took place in February 2017), the award went to:

| Category | Winner |
|----------|--------|
| **Album of the Year** | *Adele* – **_25_** |

If you had something else in mind—perhaps another genre‑specific “best album” award—I can look into those categories too!
message.reasoning:
The user asks "Who won the Grammy Award for Best Album in 2017?" They want the winner of the award category "Best Album" at the Grammys held presumably in early 2018 but awarding works from 2017. Actually the question might refer to the year 2017 awards ceremony which took place in February 2017 and awarded albums released between September 1, 2015 and August 31, 2016. But they ask specifically "in 2017". Usually people interpret as the award given during the 59th Annual Grammy Awards (held Feb 12, 2017). That was for album releases up to Aug 31, 2016.

But maybe they mean the award presented in 2017 for best album overall; i.e., the winner of the "Album of the Year" or "Record of the Year"? Wait, there is no "Best Album" category per se. There is "Album of the Year", not "Best Album." So perhaps they mis-specified. We need to clarify what exactly they meant. Could also be "Best New Artist," etc. Let's check: In 2017, the winners were:

- Record of the Year – Adele – "Hello"
- Song of the Year – Beyoncé & Jay-Z – "Formation"
- Album of the Year – Adele – "25"

So likely they asked about "Grammy Award for Best Album" meaning "Album of the Year".

Thus answer: Adele's album "25."

We should respond with clarification: There's no "Best Album" category; it's called "Album of the Year." Provide details accordingly. Also mention the year it was awarded. No tool needed.
